tags.name: Cap La Houssaye
tags.note: Shore-accessible site at the southern edge of Saint-Paul bay; depth 2-18m across reef, small caves, seagrass bed, and a submerged cannon relic at ~5m; three resident green turtles regularly seen in the seagrass at the north of the site; all levels

tags.name: Pain de Sucre
tags.note: Near Boucan Canot beach, named for a rock formation on the beach; reef platform of fissures, canyons, arches and small caves over white sand; most sources report 6-20m, one dive-blog source reports a shallower 3-12m range; popular baptism/beginner site, good for night diving and photography

tags.name: Tour de Boucan
tags.note: Reclassified reef -> pinnacle: an isolated rock tower/pinnacle off Boucan Canot rising from a 22-25m seabed (sources vary between 22m and 25m max); walls host caves, drift-prone channels and rocky canyons; Level 1/all levels

tags.name: Passe de l'Ermitage
tags.note: Reclassified reef -> drift: a channel/pass cut through the reef crest at Ermitage-les-Bains where lagoon meets open ocean (PADI's own site tag is 'Derive, Recif'); depth 6-25m; turtle and eagle-ray cleaning stations; accessible to all levels

tags.name: Hai Siang
tags.note: Former Taiwanese fishing/lobster boat, reported length ~49m, deliberately sunk in the 1980s ~3km off Les Aigrettes near Cap Homard; sits flat on white sand at 54m; build date and tonnage not documented in available sources; Level 3/technical certification required, strong currents on descent

tags.name: Navarra
tags.note: 47m fishing vessel, abandoned and seized by the French Navy, intentionally scuttled by FFESSM Reunion in early 1996 off Saint-Gilles to create an artificial reef; broke into two sections (~10m apart) during a later cyclonic swell; sources report depth between 50m and 55m; build date and tonnage not documented; Level 3 required

tags.name: Antonio Lorenzo
tags.note: 53m Chilean longliner caught illegally fishing for toothfish near Kerguelen on 1 Sept 1998, seized and towed to Port des Galets, deliberately sunk as an artificial reef on 16 Dec 1999 off Pointe des Chateaux near Saint-Leu; lies on its port side; sources report sunk/current depth between 38m and 50m (corrected from prior 50m-only estimate - majority of independently checked sources say ~40m); build date and tonnage not documented; most sources cite Level 2 minimum, one cites Level 3

name: Tombant de la Pointe au Sel

tags.name: Tombant de la Pointe au Sel
tags.note: Reef shelf off Saint-Leu descending in steps from ~25-27m before a vertical drop; sources disagree on the base depth, reporting 60m, 71m and 80m; scalloped hammerhead sharks reported seasonally (Oct-Nov per most sources); manta ray, whale shark and marlin reported as occasional passing sightings, not guaranteed; upgraded Intermediate -> Advanced given depth range and current-dependent pelagic conditions described by sources as for experienced divers

tags.name: Le Sec Jaune
tags.note: Reclassified reef -> pinnacle: an isolated rock rising to the surface off Saint-Leu, covered in yellow soft coral (tribloo's own English site name is 'The Yellow Pinnacle'); coral plateau at 5-10m overlooks a drop-off; sources report the base between 20m and 40m; Level 1 minimum

tags.name: Le Jardin des Kiosques
tags.note: External slope of the Saint-Leu coral barrier; depth 3-32m (sources range 30-32m max); crevices, tubes and overhangs; accessible from baptism level to advanced; weak current, generally good visibility

tags.name: Sea Venture
tags.note: Panamanian cargo ship reported over 80m long (one source states 86m), carrying a timber cargo, awaiting a berth in Saint-Paul bay when destabilized by the cargo and heavy weather, took on water and sank on 16 Nov 1981; all 26 crew reached shore safely; lies inverted, sources report depth between 40m and 50m; a 1997 fuel leak led to a temporary diving ban, resolved by a 1998 clean-up; build date and tonnage not documented; Level 3 required

tags.name: La Barge de Saint-Paul
tags.note: Small (~10m) barge wreck in Saint-Paul bay, ~100m from Sea Venture, resting at 22m on black basaltic sand with large anchor chains nearby; popular day and night dive; Level 2 minimum

tags.name: La Passe des Trois-Bassins
tags.note: UNRESOLVED for validation: research found only 2 independent sources (padi.com, montresdeplongee.forumactif.com) describing a pass north of Saint-Leu, 5-25m depth, coral drop-offs, rays/turtles/reef fish; below the 3-source validation threshold, so left unvalidated pending a third independent source
